title: Piercing Statue Solo #106 (데미스탯 · P25 집중형 · 단일 투명(로즈핑크 유리) · 경계 쇄골선 · 체형 colossal, statuesque chest, a · 콘로우 · 비비드오렌지 · 메이크업 파케앙트글램 · 금속 혼합 · 재질 로즈핑크 유리 · 쥬얼리 팔찌·목걸이·반지 JQ3 · 귀 보이기)
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, demi statue portrait. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips a little further below the middle of her thighs, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her thighs, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Filipina woman — warm tan skin, heavy sculpted contour and a glowing highlighter on the cheekbones, smoky bronze and gold glitter eyeshadow, dramatic long lashes, defined dark brows, large eyes with bright real catchlights, glossy coral-red lips, a bright, confident pageant smile, bold vivid tangerine-orange hair styled in cornrows braided tight against the scalp. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. Her neck, the hollows above her collarbones and the tops of her shoulders carry the same real living skin as her face: visible pores and fine skin grain, a soft sheen of natural skin oils on the highest planes, faint fine peach-fuzz hairs catching the rim light, gentle tonal variation with a natural warm flush, and the fine natural creases of a real neck — never airbrushed, never smooth like plastic. Like any real person she is slightly asymmetrical: a few small natural beauty marks and freckles scattered unevenly, one side of her neck and shoulder very slightly warmer and more freckled than the other.

Piercings: All twenty-five piercings gather mostly on the left side of her face, and the right side stays almost bare: on the left ear eight oversized pieces — a huge mixed-metal stud hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulder, a wide mixed-metal ear cuff, three smaller mixed-metal rings, two thick mixed-metal bars and a small mixed-metal stud up to the top; one small mixed-metal stud sits in the right ear; four mixed-metal pieces in a row along the outer half of the left eyebrow, alternating small rings that pass through the brow skin with the skin visible through each loop and small round ball studs sitting on the skin; two small mixed-metal rings pass through the left nostril and a thick mixed-metal septum ring hangs below the nose; a mixed-metal hoop passes through the left edge of the lower lip with a mixed-metal snake-bite ring beside it and a small mixed-metal ring at the left edge of the upper lip; a mixed-metal Medusa stud sits above the lips; a mixed-metal labret stud and a small mixed-metal ring sit on the chin; three small mixed-metal studs run along the left jaw. Each piece carries small pearls set into the metal. All jewelry is real mixed metal (yellow gold, silver, copper and rose gold, alternating piece by piece), sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Jewelry: besides the piercings she wears four to six pieces, layered of mixed-metal bracelets and bangles on both wrists; four to six pieces, layered of mixed-metal necklaces and chains resting on her neck, collarbones and upper chest; four to six pieces, layered of mixed-metal rings on her fingers, all of it real, sitting on and over the material of her body and her real neck and hair without covering her eyes, her face or her piercings.

Physique: A colossal, statuesque chest, a broad heavy torso and wide statuesque hips, both thighs clearly separate and individually shaped, all on a grand imperial scale.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — shoulders, arms, hands, chest, belly, hips and both distinct thighs — is not painted, covered or clothed but physically made of one solid transparent material, solid pale rose-pink cast glass, with soft internal swirls and tiny bubbles, deepest rose where thickest and nearly clear at every thin edge, carved as one solid sculpted mass like a statue, never hollow, with no seam and no skin anywhere, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same material. A little further below the middle of her thighs, each thigh individually curves inward and rounds off into its own smooth, deeply polished tip — the two thighs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging, fusing or tapering into a single base — no calves, no feet, nothing continues below either tip — the material simply reaching its natural end on each leg, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Transmission: everything below the collarbones is a transparent material that light passes through, while her real face, ears and neck are opaque living flesh that no light passes through. The background and its light sources are visible straight through her body, bent and tinted by the material, with bright refraction edges and soft coloured shadows. Her face stays completely opaque.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded tip is the material's own carved finish, always the clean, deliberate result of a sculpture — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a pale lilac on one side and a soft mint on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, body angled 45 degrees, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right hand gently tucking a lock of hair back behind her right ear so the ear and its piercings show clearly, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: the glowing backdrop floods her body from behind, so a pale lilac passes through one side and a soft mint passes through the other. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only; a thin cool rim light traces her whole figure. Only her face, ears and neck read as real skin. Shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
